Title: Dogged Pursuit at superior on a vampire already having one attached

Messages.Author: Nosk
Messages.Body:
If I control a vampire that has a Dogged Pursuit atteched to it. Can this vampire play Dogged Pursuit at superior to try to block another action?

What is confusing to me is that if it is played at superior there is no guarantee that it will get attached to the vampire, there is a condition for that.

Dogged Pursuit
Only usable by a locked vampire.
[ani] This vampire unlocks and attempts to block. If this vampire does not block this action, lock them after action resolution.
[ANI] As above, and if this vampire does not block this action, put this card on them after action resolution. This vampire can burn this card to get +1 intercept. A vampire can have only one Dogged Pursuit.

But the question is not about whether the dogged pursuit will be attached or not. By the text card, it is clear that if the vampire had a dogged pursuit attached, the new one cannot attached.

The question is: Can I play the card at superior if I the vampire already has a dogged attached?

If I can play it, I could use a dogged to unlock a vampire who already has a dogged on, burn the dogged already attached (not the one I just played) and in case I fail to block, the dogged I played during this action would be attached.

According to  this we could argue that the outcome of the dogged pursuit effect is not known until the block is resolved. It is actually kind of a coin flip too.

I think we should be able to play it, and when the block fails just don't attach it if the vampire already has one.

Messages.Author: mipopo3
Messages.Body:

> I can play it, I could use a dogged to unlock a vampire who already has a dogged on, burn the dogged already attached (not the one I just played) and in case I fail to block, the dogged I played during this action would be attached.

This is the correct sequence.

Vampire can play it on Superior; there is no restriction on it. But at the end of the action, if the old one was not used, the new one will not be attached in action resolution. As the attaching part is at the end of the action ( if it was successful or blocked).

This ruling is before the update and rewording, so the ruling is Mute.
Edit* however that is a new ruling with updated text  ruling

A unique ruling is that stopping a play of a card, a card stating "you can have only one," is in effect only after it's resolved and in play.

Thus, you can't play equip Blood Tears of Kephran while having Blood Tears of Kephran.
As this is a self-contest, that is stopping you from playing it.

While you can have more than one piece of the same equipment, like Magnum, Flak Jacket, nothing is stopping you from playing it, but there is nothing you can do to have two pieces of the equipment with a restriction that you can have only one.

Edit: Here is the part of the discussion that the rulebook wording should be updated to match existing rulings regarding unique cards.  discusion

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
> Oortje wrote:
> Hi, i dont understand the "outcome is unknown" argument.
> Imagine I have a wrmh talk radio in play (can lock to grant intercept to any minion, when used on not-my-minion AND block fails). Can I play a parity shift while being on the same amount of pool as anybody else? I dont know if i am able to resolve the actio.
> I know this is far fetched. I just want to know yhe arguement.
>
The "outcome is unknown" nature of an effect is only relevant for the resolution of the same effect, not distinct effects, such as WMRH and Parity Shift in your example.

The Portrait can be played even if the vampire has already bled because it has a built-in random outcome that could be legal in some cases, and illegal in some others. (It could have been ruled the other way round, both designer choices are valid).

> Sérgio wrote:
> Based on this thread, equating a self-contained ability (Gathii) with effects dependent on external factors (the need for intercept or block fails), then I should be able to:

> 3. Attempt to equip Unlicensed Taxi Cab while riding an Unlicensed Taxi Cab (so long as a Prince or Archbishop is present).
> 4. Attempt to get ANY vehicle while riding Ambulance or Unlicensed Taxi Cab.
>
No. None of these have a random outcome, and you cannot attempt to do something that would result in something illegal (such as having two Leather Jackets).

Messages.Author: Sérgio
Messages.Body:
Agreed, none of them have a random outcome. Which is why, Dogged Pursuit, which also doesn't have a random outcome, but an outcome dependent on choices made by you, should not inherit the Gathii ruling. Gathii's ability is not to provide stealth, but to flip the top card of your library; if that card happens to belong to group 1, you get X effect, otherwise, you get Y effect.

Dogged Pursuit's text neither follows that reasoning nor is it random, instead being fully controlled by the player. Given the only difference between superior and inferior is the ability to place the card on the vampire, which points towards the intent of the card's design and wording, if the check is only done upon action resolution, then there is no reason why I shouldn't be able to check only upon action resolution of Blood Tears of Kephran, or Leather Jacket - after all, they're as random as Dogged Pursuit.

What is actually being set as precedent here is a distinction between playing cards with at least partial card text being delayed conditional effects, at a point when said delayed conditional effect could not be met given current game state but might in the future, and attempting actions when their resolution is not legal given current game state but might be upon resolution. And I'm not sure those are distinguishable.
